The printed proof of (1) uses sup over a compact annulus of |d_theta tau| (l.812), and (2) needs the broken line to be rectifiable and delta bounded below on annuli: both need C^1 (a merely differentiable g can have d_theta g unbounded on compacts). findings: Both items are proved by the printed arguments, made metric: (1) a Cauchy sequence has log r Cauchy (l.799-806), hence stays in an annulus, hence theta Cauchy (l.808-821), and the coordinate limit is reached along segments; (2) by contraposition, the broken line through (r_n, theta_n) has finite length by l.838-848's bound and telescoping, so it is Cauchy and converges, which is impossible at the axis since delta is bounded below on annuli (clamp_le_edist).
B21 l.835: the interval ]r_n, r_{n+1}[ should read ]r_{n+1}, r_n[ (r_{n+1} < r_n/2).

B21 l.838-840: with the stated slope |theta'| <= 2pi/r_n one has r^2 theta'^2 <= 4pi^2, so the bound is sqrt(1 + 4pi^2 - 2 tau'), not sqrt(5 - 2 tau') (and tau' <= (1+4pi^2)/2, not 5/2). Harmless: any constant works; the formalization realigns the angles so |theta_{n+1} - theta_n| <= pi and bounds each straight piece by (1 + 2pi^2) dr - d tau (sqrt_graphQuad_le_seg).

B21 l.842 'By completeness of Sigma, the length of gamma is infinite' uses that the induced metric does not let a finite-length inextendible curve escape; for the strip this is clamp_le_edist (delta >= delta_0 > 0 on each annulus, from C^1 and periodicity).
questions: Accept the reading 'piecewise smooth' = C^1 on the strip (one piece) for Lemma 2.8 (the printed proofs need C^1; the cusp of Lemma 2.6(ii), the only use, is C^n)?
Accept the strip (universal cover of D_R^*) as the domain on which completeness of Sigma^* is read?

sorries.obstruction: The spear-local surgery is proved (spear_surgery_local: Lemma 2.6(ii) + 2.8(1) + 2.10, 0 sorry). Besides the upstream sorries (Lemma 2.3 = GXScaffold.BTZ.Spear's connectedSpace_W0, isCauchySurfaceOn_W0, globallyHyperbolic_glued, isCauchySurface_glued; Lemma 2.4's future case) three obstructions are genuine: (1) regularity: Spear's lem_add_BTZ_param_line gives the rim datum only C^0, while Lemma 2.8(1)'s delta-criterion needs a C^1 rim (B21 l.227 assumes a smooth spacelike Cauchy surface; there is no smoothing theorem for E0-manifolds); (2) curves: Remark 2.12's decomposition of an inextensible causal curve of Reg M into spear arcs with the end conditions of lem_intersect_number_complete needs the relative curve-extension theory absent from lean-causal (Spear's isCauchySurface_glued (ii) has the same gap); (3) length: IsSpacelikeLipschitz of Sigma* in Reg M's flat charts and completeness of Causal.Flat.InducedLengthSpace glued from the strip's pulled length in each spear and compactness of Sigma outside them. The library only has the density identity localDensity_chartSys_eq. The edist comparison on chart domains and the passage from the strip (a universal cover) to Sigma* cap spear are missing. regM is therefore not decomposed so that only Lemma 2.3 remains.

findings: Prop 2.17's proof (l.1089-1093) needs Sigma cap S_Delta to be a smooth (C^1) spacelike circle, which comes from the smooth spacelike Cauchy surface of the definition of Cauchy-compact (l.227), not from a topological one.
questions: Read 'Cauchy-compact' as B21 l.227 does (a smooth, at least C^1, spacelike compact Cauchy surface), so that Lemma 2.4's rim datum is C^1? Or should a smoothing step be built?

kb_proposals: FTC for a length: a Lipschitz f on [a,b] with k|f'| <= localDensity a.e. gives k|f(b)-f(a)| <= localLength (LipschitzOnWith.absolutelyContinuousOnInterval + AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.integral_deriv_eq_sub; GX.E0Surgery.le_localLength_of_lipschitzOnWith). Combined with LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt_real it turns every pointwise density bound into a PulledLength edist bound.

A path Lipschitz in charts for a single developing map F has F o gamma.extend globally Lipschitz (Causal.Flat.isLocLip_pulled_iff); read coordinates back through continuous linear functionals of Minkowski 2 and ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith on a compact box (GX.E0Surgery.path_coords).

A clamped coordinate max(r, rho) is Lipschitz with derivative r' above rho and 0 elsewhere (IsLocalMin.deriv_eq_zero at r = rho): it gives 'leaving an annulus costs length' with no first-exit-time argument (GX.E0Surgery.clamp_le_edist).

In E0, Le x y gives x.1 <= y.1 (Le.norm_sub_le) and rad x <= rad y (Le.closed.2.1): along a causal arc both tau and r are monotone, which turns the end conditions of B21 Lemma 2.10 into order-theoretic ones.
